chunks: Wuhayb ibn Hafs narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about the one for whom it is appropriate to perform the stoning at night—who is he?

He عليه السلام said: "The wood-gatherer, the owned servant who has no control over any of his affairs, the fearful, the debtor, and the sick person who is unable to stone. He is to be carried to the Jamarat, and if he is able to stone, then he should stone; otherwise, stone on his behalf while he is present."

key_terms.الْجِمَارِ: the Jamarat, the designated place for the ritual stoning in hajj
key_terms.الْحَاطِبَةُ: the wood-gatherer, one whose circumstance justifies night stoning
key_terms.الْخَائِفُ: the fearful person who has reason to avoid the regular time
key_terms.الْمَدِينُ: the debtor, listed among those granted concession
key_terms.الْمَرِيضُ: the sick person unable to carry out the rite normally
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: the servant under another's authority who lacks control over his affairs
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: at night, indicating a permitted time due to excuse
key_terms.يَرْمِيَ: to throw the pebbles in the ritual stoning

ai.seo_question: Who is permitted to stone the Jamarat at night according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning those excused to perform the stoning of the Jamarat at night during hajj. It identifies specific categories of hardship and also states that a sick person should be brought to the Jamarat if possible, or else another may stone on his behalf while he is present.
